learningObjective: Reason about the fixed hardware limits on grid and block dimensions and identify which configurations are legal.

hardwareContext.architecture: Ampere (sm_80, A100) and generally similar to modern architectures
requiredFeatures: 1024 threads/block max; 65535 grid.y/z max; 2^31 - 1 grid.x max on sm_60+

stem: For a compute-capability 8.0 (A100) GPU, which of the following kernel launch configurations is legal?

options.text: `gridDim = (1000, 1, 1)`, `blockDim = (33, 32, 1)`. Even though `33 * 32 = 1056 > 1024`, the CUDA runtime silently truncates block dimensions to the nearest multiple of 32, so the launch succeeds with `blockDim.x = 32`.
`gridDim = (1, 1, 1)`, `blockDim = (2048, 1, 1)`. This is legal because a single block can span up to 4096 threads on sm_80 as long as no shared memory is used.

`gridDim = (65535, 65535, 65535)`, `blockDim = (32, 32, 1)`. `blockDim.x * blockDim.y * blockDim.z = 1024 ≤ 1024` and all grid dims are within the 65535 (y/z) / 2^31-1 (x) hardware maximum on sm_80; this is a legal launch.
Grid dimensions on Ampere are hard-capped at 65535 across x, y, z; any request larger than 65535 in any dimension is rejected. This is why one-dimensional grids are always the safest choice.

explanation: On compute capability 8.0 (A100): max threads per block = 1024; max blockDim = (1024, 1024, 64); max gridDim.x = 2^31 - 1 (~2.1B); max gridDim.y = max gridDim.z = 65535. A: `32*32*1 = 1024` (at the limit) and grid dims fit. Legal. B: `2048 > 1024`, exceeds threads-per-block cap; illegal. C: nvcc/runtime does not silently truncate; the launch returns an error at `cudaGetLastError`. D: gridDim.x is not capped at 65535 on sm_60+; it is capped at 2^31 - 1.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: no silent truncation; launch fails.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: at the block-threads limit and within grid dim limits.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: gridDim.x cap is 2^31-1 on sm_60+.

assumptions: sm_80 (A100) launch limits as documented in CUDA guide.
nonImplications: Does not imply the maximum legal launch is efficient; huge grids may hit resource contention.
Does not imply block dim limits are architecture-uniform; some architectures have lower caps.
